answer: First reported (BLS Employment Situation, April 4, 2025): total nonfarm payrolls rose by 228,000 in March 2025, seasonally adjusted (159,398 thousand vs 159,170 thousand for February in that vintage). The data now (FRED series PAYEMS, read October 10, 2026, with data through September 2026) show a gain of 67,000 (158,377 thousand in March vs 158,310 thousand in February 2025). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed); the changes are my subtraction of the published levels.

First reported (BLS Employment Situation, June 6, 2025): total nonfarm payrolls rose by 139,000 in May 2025, seasonally adjusted (159,561 thousand vs 159,422 thousand for April in that vintage). The data now (FRED series PAYEMS, read October 10, 2026) show a gain of 13,000 (158,498 thousand in May vs 158,485 thousand in April 2025). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed); the changes are my subtraction of the published levels.

First reported (BLS Employment Situation, July 3, 2025): total nonfarm payrolls rose by 147,000 in June 2025, seasonally adjusted (159,724 thousand vs 159,577 thousand for May in that vintage). The data now (FRED series PAYEMS, read October 10, 2026) show a loss of 20,000 jobs (158,478 thousand in June vs 158,498 thousand in May 2025). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed); the changes are my subtraction of the published levels.

First reported (BLS Employment Situation, August 1, 2025): total nonfarm payrolls rose by 73,000 in July 2025, seasonally adjusted (159,539 thousand vs 159,466 thousand for June in that vintage). The data now (FRED series PAYEMS, read October 10, 2026) show a gain of 64,000 (158,542 thousand in July vs 158,478 thousand in June 2025). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed); the changes are my subtraction of the published levels.

The advance estimate (BEA, April 28, 2022) put real GDP growth in Q1 2022 at -1.4% (seasonally adjusted annual rate, change from the prior quarter). The current data (FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA, read October 10, 2026) show -1.0%. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed).

The advance estimate (BEA, July 28, 2022) put real GDP growth in Q2 2022 at -0.9% (seasonally adjusted annual rate, change from the prior quarter). The current data (FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA, read October 10, 2026) show +0.6%, so the originally reported decline is now a small increase. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed).

The advance estimate (BEA, January 30, 2025) put real GDP growth in Q4 2024 at 2.3% (seasonally adjusted annual rate, change from the prior quarter). The current data (FRED series A191RL1Q225SBEA, read October 10, 2026) show 2.4%. Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed).

4.0%, for January 2025 (seasonally adjusted, U-3). That was the latest month available as of March 1, 2025; the February 2025 figure had not yet been published. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via the ALFRED March 1, 2025 vintage of series UNRATE (St. Louis Fed).

159,536 thousand (about 159.5 million) jobs, seasonally adjusted, for December 2024. That is the figure as it stood on February 1, 2025, before the annual benchmark revision published later that month. Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via the ALFRED February 1, 2025 vintage of series PAYEMS (St. Louis Fed). For comparison, the same month is now shown as 158,316 thousand.

About 2.9% both then and now. As first reported (BLS, January 15, 2025), the seasonally adjusted CPI-U all-items index was 317.685 for December 2024 against 308.742 for December 2023, a 12-month rise of 2.90%. The current data (FRED series CPIAUCSL, read October 10, 2026) show 317.604 against 308.741, a rise of 2.87%, which still rounds to 2.9%. The percentages are my calculation from the published index levels (1982-84=100). Source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, via FRED/ALFRED (St. Louis Fed).
